paper_sections.title: Post-traumatic stress symptoms correlate with smaller subgenual cingulate, caudate, and insula volumes in unmedicated combat veterans
Covariation for combat exposure, depressive symptoms, and age

description.value: The study examined whether post-traumatic stress symptom severity and trauma exposure were associated with regional gray matter volume in combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, and compared veterans with and without PTSD.

design.value: Cross-sectional structural MRI study of 28 combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans. Gray matter was analyzed using voxel-based morphometry with dimensional regressions against total CAPS score and childhood and adult trauma load, followed by secondary cluster-level regressions and a voxel-wise PTSD versus non-PTSD group contrast.

name.value: standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template

description.value: Past month post-traumatic stress symptoms were assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale; total CAPS score and B, C, and D symptom subscores were used.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I)

description.value: Subjects were assessed with the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders to determine psychiatric diagnoses and comorbidities.
Depressive symptom severity was measured using the Beck Depression Inventory.
Level of combat exposure was measured with the Combat Exposure Scale.

The Trauma History Questionnaire was used as a self-report measure of exposure to a wide variety of traumas, including the number of times an event occurred and age at exposure; the number of trauma types before and after age 18 was summed as childhood and adult trauma load.

source_definition.value: Past month PTSS were assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS).
The number of trauma types experienced before age 18, defined as the number of THQ questions positively endorsed, was summed to indicate childhood trauma load.
The number of trauma types experienced after age 18, defined as the number of THQ questions positively endorsed, was summed to indicate adult trauma load.
Total gray matter volume (GMV) as determined by Easy Volume.
Level of combat exposure was measured with the Combat Exposure Scale.
Depressive symptom severity was measured using the Beck Depression Inventory.
Age was added as an additional regressor against extracted average cluster values.

association_direction.value: moderately inverse with the left insula cluster

source_definition.value: Subjects were categorized by diagnosis of PTSD versus non-PTSD.

description.value: Twenty-eight combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, including 25 males and 3 females, were recruited from the Pittsburgh area.

inclusion_criteria.value: DD Form 214 documentation of prior military service was obtained from all potential participants.

exclusion_criteria.value: History of traumatic brain injury or neurological disease.
Current (past month) alcohol or illicit substance abuse or dependence.
Use of greater than 14 alcoholic drinks per week over the past month, confirmed on prospective diaries.
Failure to meet screening criteria for MRI, including the presence of metal clips, heart pacemakers, claustrophobia, and possibility of pregnancy for women of child-bearing age.

recruitment_method.value: Recruited from the Pittsburgh area through public media advertisements.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I)

clinical_characteristics.value: Thirteen subjects met full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria. One subject also met criteria for generalized anxiety disorder in the past month. No other concurrent psychiatric illnesses were identified.

description.value: Veterans who met full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria.

inclusion_criteria.value: Met full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria.

clinical_characteristics.value: Thirteen subjects met full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria.

description.value: Combat-exposed veterans who did not meet criteria for PTSD.

inclusion_criteria.value: Did not meet criteria for PTSD.

clinical_characteristics.value: Fifteen subjects were classified as non-PTSD.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Siemens Trio MRI scanner (Siemens, Malvern, PA) at the University of Pittsburgh Magnetic Resonance Research Center

description.value: Three-dimensional sagittal high-resolution MPRAGE scans were acquired with echo time = 2.98 ms, repetition time = 2300 ms, slice thickness = 1.2 mm, 160 slices, flip angle = 9°, field of view = 256 × 240 mm, inversion time = 900 ms, and image matrix = 256 × 240, covering the entire brain.

DICOM structural images were converted to NIFTI-1 format, segmented into gray and white matter, normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8, modulated by Jacobian determinants derived from spatial normalization, resampled to 2 × 2 × 2 mm, and smoothed with a 12-mm Gaussian kernel. For hippocampus-only analysis, images were smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: DICOM files were converted to NIFTI-1 format.
Converted files were segmented into gray and white matter.
Images were normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8.
Standard SPM values were selected to bias regularization (0.0001) and full width at half-maximum cutoff (60 mm).
Voxel values were modulated by the Jacobian determinants derived from spatial normalization.
The final voxel resolution after normalization was 2 × 2 × 2 mm.
Images were smoothed with a 12-mm Gaussian kernel.
For analysis of the hippocampus only, images were smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: Processed gray matter images were analyzed in a multiple regression model within SPM8. Regressors included the total past-month CAPS score, childhood trauma load, and adult trauma load. All images were covaried for total gray matter volume as determined by Easy Volume.

Extracted cluster averages adjusted for total GMV were analyzed in SPSS. Current depression scores from the BDI and age were added as additional regressors; normalized cluster averages were also entered into a multivariate regression with CAPS symptom subscores B, C, and D. For additional multivariate regressions, Bonferroni correction was applied based on the number of clusters examined (P < 0.05/4 or 0.013).

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), version 18

model_settings.value: A voxel-wise group contrast was conducted within SPM8 by dividing subjects into diagnostic groups of PTSD (n = 13) and non-PTSD (n = 15), with total GMV as a covariate.
For Pearson/Spearman correlations and t-tests in SPSS, results were considered significant at P < 0.05, two-tailed.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), version 18

role.value: greater gray matter volume relative to the non-PTSD group

definition.value: Contrast between these two groups, PTSD and non-PTSD, with total GMV as a covariate

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

model_representation_notes.value: Total gray matter volume was included as a covariate.

interpretations.value: The dimensional analysis suggests that these neural changes are specific to PTSS and likely occur even below the diagnostic threshold of PTSD.

caption.value: Summary of smaller gray matter volume associated with greater post-traumatic stress symptoms (↑CAPS, ↓GMV), greater child trauma load (↑Child Trauma, ↓GMV), or PTSD compared to non-PTSD.

footer.value: Regions shown were significant at uncorrected P < 0.001, threshold k = 50 voxels. k = cluster size. CAPS = Clinician-administered PTSD Scale. GMV = gray matter volume. Peak coordinates based on Montreal Neurological Institute atlas.

description.value: Regional gray matter findings for the symptom regression, childhood trauma load regression, and PTSD versus non-PTSD group contrast.
